title: Help
subtitle: How to add the Claude and IGDB keys, how the stats are calculated and where updates come from.

claude.title: Assistant: adding your Claude key
claude.body:
The assistant uses **Claude**, by Anthropic. Each person uses their own API key: questions are billed to your Anthropic account, not to whoever installed the app.

### 1. Create an account and add credit
1. Open the [Anthropic Console](https://console.anthropic.com) and create an account (or sign in).
2. Under **Billing**, add credit. The API is paid separately: a Claude.ai subscription (Pro or Max) doesn’t include API access.

### 2. Create the key
1. In the console, open **API Keys** and click **Create Key**.
2. Name it (for example "GameTracker Vault") and copy the key. It starts with `sk-ant-` and is shown **only once**.

### 3. Add the key to the app
1. Open [Settings → Assistant](/Vault/Settings#assistant).
2. Paste the key into **API key**.
3. Click **Load my account’s models** and pick a model (see "Which model to pick").
4. Click **Save**. The app tests the key with Anthropic before saving it; if it’s rejected, it isn’t saved.

Then open the [Assistant](/Vault/Assistant) and ask away.

### What Claude sees
With each question, the app sends Anthropic the chat and your shelf: game names, statuses, hours, 1–10 ratings, dates and your written notes. That’s what lets it recommend games based on what you played. To answer about specific games, it can also search IGDB.

### Security
- The key is **encrypted** on the server and never comes back to the browser; only its last 4 characters are shown.
- Nobody else uses your key, not even the administrator through the app.
- To stop using it, click **Remove key**. If you think the key was exposed, delete it in the Anthropic Console too.

models.title: Which model to pick
models.body:
The list shows the models your key can use. The main ones:

- **Claude Sonnet** (for example `claude-sonnet-5-5`): the balance of quality, speed and price. **Recommended** for everyday use.
- **Claude Opus** (for example `claude-opus-5-5`): the most capable, for more thoughtful recommendations and long chats. Slower and pricier.
- **Claude Haiku** (for example `claude-haiku-5-5`): the fastest and cheapest, good for short questions.

Pricing is by the amount of text (tokens) sent and received. Since each question includes your shelf, a big shelf costs a bit more per question. Current prices are at [anthropic.com/pricing](https://www.anthropic.com/pricing).

You can switch models any time in [Settings → Assistant](/Vault/Settings#assistant) without entering the key again.

stats.title: How the stats are calculated
stats.body:
[Stats](/Vault/Stats) does the maths on your shelf.

**Hours.** If you logged a game’s hours, those count. If you didn’t and the game is finished, the **IGDB player average** for that kind of finish counts instead:
- main story: the average main-story time;
- with side content: the average time for the story plus side content;
- 100%: the average time to do everything.

These estimated hours are striped and marked "estimated", so they never get mixed up with yours. Games in progress, paused or dropped without logged hours don’t count, since there’s no way to know how long you played: log the hours on the game page to include them.

**Up next.** Adds up the average main-story time of games marked "Later".

**Completion rate.** Of the games you stopped playing (finished or dropped), the share you finished.

Genres and average times come from IGDB and refresh once a week.

shelf.title: The shelf and the random pick
shelf.body:
On each game’s page, the **My shelf** panel (on the right) keeps what you did with it:

- **Status**: in progress (playing, paused, later, dropped) or finished (main story, with side content, 100%). Clicking the chosen status again unselects it.
- **Progress**: hours played and start and finish dates.
- **Review**: your 1–10 rating and written notes.

Nothing is saved until you click **Save**; **Undo** goes back to what’s saved.

On [Home](/Vault) your games sit on four shelves. Under **Not sure what to play?**, "From my list" picks at random among your later and paused games, and "Discover a new one" brings a well-rated game from IGDB that you don’t have yet.

account.title: Account and users
account.body:
In [Settings → Account](/Vault/Settings#account) you change your **name** and **password** (the password needs the current one).

New accounts are created in [Admin](/Vault/Admin) with **New user** (administrators only). There the administrator can also edit an account (name, role and a new password) or delete it; that person’s shelf and assistant key are deleted with it. There must always be at least one administrator.

igdb.title: Game catalogue: adding the IGDB key
igdb.body:
Search, game pages, average times and covers come from **IGDB** (by Twitch). There’s one key for the whole installation, added by an administrator.

### 1. Create the application on Twitch
1. Sign in to [dev.twitch.tv/console](https://dev.twitch.tv/console) with a Twitch account. The account needs **two-factor authentication** turned on.
2. Open **Applications** and click **Register Your Application**.
3. Fill in **Name** (a unique name, for example "gametracker-vault-home"), **OAuth Redirect URLs** with `http://localhost`, **Category** "Application Integration" and **Client Type** **Confidential**.
4. Click **Create**.

### 2. Copy the credentials
1. In the list, open the application with **Manage**.
2. Copy the **Client ID**.
3. Click **New Secret** and copy the **Client Secret** (shown only once).

### 3. Add them to the app
1. Open [Admin](/Vault/Admin), in the **Game catalogue (IGDB)** card.
2. Paste the Client ID and Client Secret and click **Save**.
3. Click **Test connection** to confirm.

The secret is encrypted on the server and never comes back to the browser. To change it, generate a new one on Twitch and paste it here; the old one stops working.

IGDB is free for **non-commercial** use. Commercial use needs an agreement with Twitch.

code.title: Code and updates (GitHub)
code.body:
The app’s code is public on **GitHub**, at [github.com/TTiagoSousa/gametrackervault](https://github.com/TTiagoSousa/gametrackervault). The Proxmox installation clones that repository and updates come from there.

### Branches
- `develop`: where work happens; may be unstable.
- `staging`: the next version, for testing.
- `main`: the stable version, installed by default.

Changes move from `develop` to `staging` and then to `main`.

### Versions
Each version is a **tag** `vX.Y.Z` on `main`, with notes in `releases/<version>/` in Portuguese, English and Spanish. The app finds new tags by itself: they show up in [Admin](/Vault/Admin), in the **Version** card and on the **Versions** page, with notes in your language, and the administrator updates with one click. It never goes back to an older version.

### Installing from a private fork
The official repository is public and needs no token. If you install from a private copy of your own (`REPO_URL`), the installation needs a read-only token:
1. On GitHub, open **Settings** → **Developer settings** → **Personal access tokens** → **Fine-grained tokens** → **Generate new token**.
2. Pick only that repository and, under **Repository permissions**, set **Contents** to **Read-only**.
3. Generate it and copy it (shown only once).
4. When creating the container, answer **No** to "Is the repository public?" and paste the token.

The token is stored in the repository address inside the container (`/opt/gametracker`) and is used to fetch new versions. If it is deleted or expires, updates stop working until you add a new one.

### Container commands
- `gametracker-update`: updates to the latest version, with a backup and a rollback if anything fails.
- `gametracker-config`: changes the server settings.

android.title: Android app
android.body:
The Android app opens GameTracker Vault full screen, with its own icon, like any other app on your phone. It connects to your server: everything you do in the app is the same as on the site, and it updates by itself when the server is updated.

### Install
1. On your phone, open this page and tap **Download APK** (above).
2. Open the downloaded file. If Android warns you, allow **installing apps from this source** (the browser or the file manager) and go back.
3. Tap **Install**.

The app doesn't come from the Play Store, so Android may warn that it's from an unknown source — that's normal for apps installed by hand.

### First time
1. Open the **GameTracker Vault** app.
2. Type your server's address, the same one you use in the browser (for example `https://gametracker.example.com`), and tap **Connect**. The app checks that the address really is a GameTracker Vault.
3. Sign in with your username and password.

### Day to day
- Android's **Back** button goes to the previous page.
- Outside links (videos, IGDB, the Anthropic console…) open in the browser.
- With no connection you get **Can’t reach the server** with **Try again**.
- To use another server: avatar menu → **Change server**.

### Updating the app
The app’s content always comes from the server: when you update the server, the app shows the new version straight away. The APK itself only changes when the phone side changes (connect screen, icon…) and has its own version.

From version 1.1.0, the app checks the server for a new APK every time it opens and asks **Update / Later**. Updating downloads it and asks Android to install it — just confirm (the first time, Android asks you to allow installing apps from GameTracker Vault). You can also check here with **Check for updates**. Your session and server stay saved.

Version 1.0.0 can’t update itself yet: install 1.1.0 by hand once (download it and install over the old one).
